issues: Duplicate implementation (AGENTS.md reuse/remove-duplicates), and the duplicate has the junction data-loss hazard that B1 was designed around. poly_apps/laravel_main/app/Apps/ServerManagerV1/ServerManagerV1Utils/ServerManagerV1ElevatedAccess.php:238-262 `nativeRmdir` is an older native recursive delete for non-Linux hosts. Its only caller is deletePathWithSudo :199-204, used by the site purge ServerManagerV1NginxManagerCtl.php:651. The fix added a second one (FileSystemManager::deleteNative) in the same owner's scope and left nativeRmdir in place. nativeRmdir recurses on `is_dir($full) && !is_link($full)` (:257) and scans the top level after `is_link||is_file` fails (:241-249). On PHP 8.5/Windows a junction reports is_link=false and an inconsistent is_dir=true, so purging a web root that contains a junction (for example to a build dir) deletes the target's files. Linux `rm -rf` does not follow links, so this is also a parity gap. The leader's round-2 claims 'No second native recursive delete exists' and 'No junction-safe helper exists in app/' rest on a grep for CHILD_FIRST|filetype( that cannot match a scandir-based walk. Fix (pycore-laravel scope only): at :202 replace `self::nativeRmdir($path)` with `\App\Utils\FileSystemManager::delete($path)`, and delete nativeRmdir (:238-262). The purge guard (NginxManagerCtl :636-638) rejects paths under core_node, so mapExternalPath is the identity for these paths. The Windows branch then reaches deleteNative, and the return contract (true when the path is gone) is unchanged. Verify: php -l on both files; grep shows no nativeRmdir left; an in-process scratch call of ServerManagerV1ElevatedAccess::deletePathWithSudo(<scratch dir holding a nested junction and a file>, '') returns success, removes the dir and leaves the junction target intact (print the *_created flags).
